modules.name: Client independence, built in rather than stripped out
leaf_texts: Sweep refusing any client name, domain, work address, company id or storage path literal in src, migrations, console and compose
One settings module as the only place a client-specific value is read, so nothing reads the environment directly
Every client-specific value an environment variable with a declared default, a documented meaning and a refusal when it is missing
Branding as configuration: company name, logo, colours, product name, sender address
Identity provider as configuration: realm, issuer, client id, redirect URIs, brokered directory
Model and provider choice as configuration, including a local-only profile with no external provider
Storage, object store and vector store locations as configuration
The sweep runs in CI on every commit, so the final audit verifies a gate that has been green all along rather than cleaning a year of drift
Test: the application boots and answers a question configured as a fictitious company with no Verz value present
Migrations build every schema, table, index, constraint, trigger and row-level security policy from an empty database
Generic demo seed: a fictitious company, departments, people and records, deliberately not the Verz test fixture
No install step depends on a Verz database, dump, backup or export
First-run setup creating the first administrator, with no default password anywhere
CI job installing from empty into a scratch container and asking one question end to end
Uninstall and data-return procedure, because a client who leaves must be able to take their data and leave nothing behind
Starter pack loaded at install: the six roles, standard permission sets, the standard agents and sensible defaults, so a new client opens a furnished system rather than a blank one
Starter pack is separate from the demo seed, because a client wants the roles and not the fictitious records
The repository is the template and a client install is a release tag plus one environment file, so a fix reaches every client rather than one copy
No duplicated repository anywhere, because a copy diverges the first time a bug is fixed in one and not the other and nothing says so
Repository structure a reader can navigate: what is application, what is configured per client, what is never edited, where migrations, scripts and documentation live
Verz is one deployment: its values live in a per-install file and never in this repository

On a scratch install a handover exports every store and the audit ledger in open formats with a manifest the company can check, then removes the identity realm, bucket, vault secrets, schedules, route, containers and configuration, revokes connector authorisations and the chat app, and issues a certificate naming the date the last backup expires

modules.name: Client deployment template
leaf_texts: Per-client variables in a separate private repository, one file per install, documented field by field
Secrets minted per install and never copied between clients, enforced by a check that refuses a shared value
One published image deployed by tag, never rebuilt per client
Release pinning per client, so one client can hold a version back without forking
Server requirements and a recommended specification per profile, with the memory and connection arithmetic already measured
Operating system, runtime, package and port requirements
Step-by-step install from a clean server, written so it needs no reference to the Verz install
Domain, DNS, reverse proxy, TLS and firewall setup
Configuration guide: every value a new client must set, in one table, with where each comes from
Integration guide per connector, including what each one is trusted to read
Authentication and administrator setup, including the staff source choice
Backup, monitoring, logging and health-check configuration
Troubleshooting guide built from the failures actually hit during this build, symptom first
Update procedure and rollback procedure, both rehearsed rather than written
Install script, idempotent and safe to run twice
Environment template generator that refuses to emit a value it cannot explain
Database create, migrate and seed scripts
Health-check script a person runs after deploying and can read the output of
Backup and restore scripts, with the restore verified rather than assumed
Update script pinning a release tag, and a rollback script re-pinning the previous one
Deployment checklist: pre-deployment, server, application, database, environment, integrations, security, testing, go-live and post-deployment
A published release for every fix, with plain-English notes stating what changed, whether it changes the database, and how urgent it is
The console shows the running version and whether a newer release exists, because nothing else reminds a client IT team to update
Audit source, configuration, compose, environment files and git history for any remaining client-specific value
Audit the database, logs, uploads, object store, vector store, embeddings and caches
Audit credentials, tokens, webhooks, third-party integrations and default administrator accounts
Verz is client number one: their live system is installed from the template by running the installer on their server, not migrated from the development environment
Verify on that install: it boots, sign-in works, the administrator works, core features answer and integrations configure, with nothing carried over from the development environment
Record the measured time from bare server to first answered question, because that number is what the template is for

A second install on a throwaway server as a fictitious client, run start to finish by somebody following only the documentation, because Verz succeeding proves the installer works for the person who wrote it
Every question asked during those two installs becomes a line in the documentation, since a question asked twice is a missing step
install.sh: one command on a fresh server that checks the machine, installs what is missing, downloads the release, builds the database and starts everything
Every password, key and secret generated on the client server during install, never defaulted and never shipped in the template
A setup code printed once by the installer and required by the first wizard screen, so whoever loads the page first cannot claim the system
Setup wizard in the console: numbered steps with visible progress, step 3 of 10, and a back button on every screen
Wizard step: company name, logo upload and web address
Wizard step: the first administrator, who becomes the Super Admin
Wizard step: staff source, choosing between Google Workspace, Microsoft, Lark or a spreadsheet, signing in and pulling the list
Wizard step: AI provider, either their own key or a local-only profile with no external provider
Wizard step: optional data source connections, skippable and repeatable later from the console
Wizard step: review everything before any of it is written, because a wizard that commits each screen as it goes cannot be corrected
The wizard becomes unreachable the moment the first administrator exists, so the install path cannot be replayed by anybody who finds the address
A resumable install: closing the browser halfway continues where it stopped rather than starting the server again
Every step validates before it advances and says what is wrong in words the person can act on
A finishing screen that hands the person straight into the console already signed in, with nothing further to configure before the system answers a question
Installer output legible to a person: what it is doing, how far through it is, and what to do if a step fails
Wizard step: chat and email channels, each connected and sent a test message before the finish, skippable and repeatable later from the console
The installer is run start to finish on a fresh AWS instance and on a fresh VPS, each ending with the company's Brain answering a question, with the time taken recorded
The administrative console is built by the release and served by the install, so an administrator has an address to open rather than a repository to build
The setup wizard writes what it collects, so a first install needs no hand-edited environment file for the values it asks for
A question can be asked and its answer read in the console, so an install proves itself end to end before any channel is connected
Console screens for skills: add a skill, see what it is trusted to reach, and assign it to an agent
Console screens for connectors: connect one, hold its credential in the vault, and see what it is trusted to read
A helper for a person who does not use a terminal: it asks for the server address and runs the one install command there
The first real release is published and fetched back on a clean machine, so the image and the archive are known to exist rather than known to be built

The rule for what belongs to the product and what belongs to one company is written into the repository's own instructions, with worked examples, and a commit that came from a staging problem has to say why its fix is generic
The install health check reports whether the host exposes kernel virtualisation, and the browser isolation stated to the administrator is taken from that result rather than assumed

The release lifecycle is proved on an install: a CI-built, signed image that passed lint, types, tests, canaries and the licence check is pulled by digest with no inbound access, migrations run before traffic, in-flight work including a running workflow drains without loss, an unnamed image is refused, rollback to the previous release completes, and the copied-deployment check passes, with the checks recorded
The release image and archive carry the licence notice of every bundled third-party component and font, generated from the lockfiles, and a release missing one fails
The release archive carries the backup and restore scripts and the installer schedules the nightly backup, so an install made from a release backs itself up without a file copied from the repository

The owner's install runs the standard profile, and the System health screen shows the worker, the vault, the object store and the connection pooler each ready, with the provider key held in the vault and not in the environment file
The owner's install is pinned to a published release tag rather than the latest image, and the Version screen shows that tag and whether a newer release exists
Every other requirement in the requirements register is demonstrated on an install by a person, and each check is recorded against the requirement it proves

Probed from an address outside the allowlist, the install answers only on its public ports with valid TLS, every administrative console refuses sign-in, and a certificate within fourteen days of expiry alerts a named person
